title: Kyiv
summary: Kyiv, the capital and largest city of Ukraine, is situated in the north-central region of the country along both banks of the Dnieper River. With a population of 2,952,301 as of January 2022, it serves as a significant industrial, scientific, educational, and cultural hub in Ukraine and Eastern Europe.

sections.heading: Geography and Demographics
paragraphs: Kyiv is located in the north-central part of [[ukraine|Ukraine]], straddling both banks of the [[dnieper|Dnieper River]]. As of January 2022, the city's population was recorded at 2,952,301, making it the seventh-most populous city in Europe.

sections.heading: Historical Significance
paragraphs: Kyiv is one of the oldest cities in [[eastern-europe|Eastern Europe]], believed to have existed as early as the 5th century. It was a commercial center along a significant trade route between Scandinavia and Constantinople and became the capital of [[kievan-rus|Kievan Rus]]', the first East Slavic state, under Varangian rule in the mid-9th century.
The city faced significant destruction during the Siege of Kiev in 1240, which led to a long period of decline in its influence.
Kyiv regained prominence during the 16th century as a center of Eastern Orthodox learning and later prospered during the Industrial Revolution of the late 19th century.

sections.heading: Political Developments
paragraphs: In 1918, following the October Revolution, the [[ukrainian-peoples-republic|Ukrainian People's Republic]] declared independence from the Russian Republic, and Kyiv became its capital. After a series of conflicts, including the [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]]-Soviet and Polish-Soviet wars, Kyiv was established as the capital of the [[ukrainian-soviet-socialist-republic|Ukrainian SSR]] in 1934.
The city suffered extensive damage during World War II but recovered to become the third-largest city in the Soviet Union.

sections.heading: Post-Soviet Era
paragraphs: Following Ukraine's independence in 1991, Kyiv has continued to be the largest and wealthiest city in the country, transitioning towards a market economy and electoral democracy. Despite losing its reliance on the armaments industry, the growth of the services and finance sectors has supported urban development.

sections.heading: Cultural and Educational Hub
paragraphs: Kyiv is recognized as an important industrial, scientific, educational, and cultural center in Ukraine, housing numerous high-tech industries, higher education institutions, and historical landmarks. The city is also served by an extensive public transport network, including the [[kyiv-metro|Kyiv Metro]].
